subject: Readout: QBR 3-Week Runway — Wins, Capacity Risks, and Decision Requests
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Readout: QBR 3-Week Runway — Wins, Capacity Risks, and Decision Requests

Team —

Quick readout ahead of the QBR run this week. TL;DR: two solid delivery wins, one capacity risk that needs a short-term decision, and two asks for leadership input.

Wins
- Finished the Dedicated autoscaler rollout for eu-west region; early telemetry shows 12% less tail latency for 99th pct requests from enterprise customers.
- Completed migration of Acme Corp’s staging traffic to our latest quantized runtime without regression (validated on shared eval set).

OKR check (selected)
- OKR: Reduce median inference latency for interactive tier to <=40ms by EOY — current progress: 46% of target achieved (perf work + quantization).
- OKR: Improve unit cost (hosted API) by 10% — current run rate: 8% improvement vs baseline, trending toward target with caching tweaks.

Capacity risk and ask
- Forecast: Acme PoC + two new enterprise trials will push peak GPU utilization above committed capacity for two 48-hour windows in the next 2 weeks (expected dates: Jun 10–11 and Jun 16–17). If unmitigated, we expect transient client errors and elevated latency impacting SLAs for a small set of paying customers.
- Decision request: Approve a time-boxed burst allocation (reserved extra capacity) for up to 48 hours on each window. Estimated incremental cost: ~$145k for both windows (Finance has preliminary numbers).
- Secondary ask: Temporary prioritization policy to route critical enterprise traffic (top 5 customers by ARR) to reserved capacity during the windows.

Other asks
1) Laura/Finance — confirm we can absorb the $145k incremental cost against Q3 run-rate or recommend reallocation (Rishi suggests tapping hiring contingency).
2) Jonas/Infra — sign-off on the prioritization policy and quick enable plan (we'll need a canary and rollback timeframe).

Attachments: qbr_runway_v3.pdf (summary deck), capacity_model.xlsx (breakdown of cost modeling).

I'll be on standby if you want to walk through the deck before the ops check on Wednesday.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP Product, Redwood Inference
---
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Readout: QBR 3-Week Runway — Wins, Capacity Risks, and Decision Requests

Rishi —

Thanks for the concise readout. Two clarifying asks before we greenlight anything on cost:
- Can Finance provide the $145k split by invoice timing (one-time vs amortized monthly)? I want visibility on Q3 impact vs run-rate.
- Are there any contractual implications with Acme (PO / amendment) if we move them to reserved capacity temporarily?

If Finance confirms the numbers look OK, I'm inclined to approve the burst given the SLA risk. Jonas — can you provide the rollback plan (max 6 hours) and post-incident telemetry window?

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Readout: QBR 3-Week Runway — Wins, Capacity Risks, and Decision Requests

Rishi / Laura —

I reviewed the capacity_model.xlsx and ran the burst simulation. Options:
1) Soft approach (preferred): enable auto-burst pool + enforce a strict QoS priority for top 5 enterprise customers. This requires a config flip, no infra deploys, and an on-call monitoring recipe. Rollback: immediate de-prioritization of the pool; expected stabilization within 30–90 minutes.
2) Hard approach: provision dedicated GPUs for the windows and steer traffic (cleaner isolation, higher cost, longer provisioning ~4–6 hours).

Recommended: move forward with option 1 for the Jun 10–11 window and keep option 2 as contingency. I'll create a canary run on Jun 9 at 02:00 PT against non-prod traffic and validate KV cache behavior.

Action items I can own:
- Implement prioritization policy and canary (Jonas) — target: Jun 9 02:00 PT
- Instrument post-window telemetry workbook and inject alerts for SLA drift (Marissa)
- Finance note requested from Laura — need sign-off by EOD Jun 8 to proceed.

Attachment: capacity_model.xlsx (updated with simulation results).

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Infrastructure

We don't need a contract amendment for a short, time-boxed reserved allocation; our PO already covers temporary capacity add-ons (per §4.2). I can confirm via email if you need written approval (happy to do that).

Thanks all — update and decisions: 

1) Finance (Laura) confirmed we can shift $160k from hiring contingency to cover the two 48-hour burst windows (final number after small adjustments). Approved for time-boxed use only.
2) We will proceed with Jonas’s option 1 (auto-burst + prioritization) for Jun 10–11. Jonas will run the canary Jun 9 02:00 PT. Marissa will own post-window telemetry and hold a 1-hour review on Jun 12 10:00 PT.
3) Acme: Emma confirmed no contract amendment needed. Emma will send email confirmation of PO coverage.

Next steps
- Jonas: flip the prioritization policy at canary and provide rollback playbook (expected 30–90m).
- Marissa: publish post-run telemetry workbook and a short incident summary (if any).
- Rishi/Product: I’ll call out the temporary prioritization in the QBR slide and highlight the runway trade-offs.

Closing the decision lane on the burst. I've attached the final QBR deck (qbr_runway_v3.pdf) and the cost model for the record.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP Product, Redwood Inference
